statements.label: thm:main
statements.title: Arithmetic orientation and harmonic realization
statements.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic orientation and harmonic realization]
\label{thm:main}
\claimid{MAIN-1}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The function field of Hitchin's ordered-icosahedron incidence cover is
\[
 \Q(\mathbf P(H))\bigl(\sqrt{5J_0}\bigr),
\qquad J_0|_V=16\sigma_3^2.
\]
Hence its restriction to \(D(\sigma_3)\subset\mathbf P(V)\) is the constant
golden torsor
\[
 D(\sigma_3)\times_{\Spec\Q}\Spec\Q(\sqrt5)
 \longrightarrow D(\sigma_3).
\]
The explicit fibre over \(xyz\) has good reduction at \(11\): its Galois
exchanger reduces to the nontrivial class
\[
 T_{11}=\operatorname{PGL}_2(11)/\operatorname{PSL}_2(11),
\]
while an explicit \(A_5\)-equivariant identification places the signed
matching cubic on the line \(\langle\sigma_3\rangle\).
\item The zonal degree-six harmonics on the ten axes through opposite
icosahedral faces contain \(V\) as their Petersen \((-2)\)-eigenspace.
Label the unit face axes by pairs \(\{i,j\}\), and put
\[
 F_y(\omega)=\sum_{i<j}(y_i+y_j)P_6(u_{ij}\mathbin{\cdot}\omega),
 \qquad
 P_6(s)=\frac{231s^6-315s^4+105s^2-5}{16}.
\]
On this four-space the spherical Gaunt cubic is
\[
 \frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}F_y(\omega)^3\,d\omega
 =-\frac{784000}{1247103}\sigma_3(y).
\]
Equivalently, the Clebsch cubic line is the four-channel restriction of the
standard degree-six Steinhardt cubic.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

statements.label: lem:localized-odd
statements.title: Localized odd generator
statements.tex:
\begin{lemma}[Localized odd generator]
\label{lem:localized-odd}
\claimid{ALG-1}.
Assume that \(2\) is invertible in \(R\), and let \(C\in R^-\) be nonzero.
After localizing at \(C^2\),
\[
 R[(C^2)^{-1}]
 =
 R^+[(C^2)^{-1}]
 \oplus
 C\,R^+[(C^2)^{-1}].
\]
\end{lemma}

statements.label: thm:rational-cover
statements.title: Rational Hitchin--Clebsch cover
statements.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Rational Hitchin--Clebsch cover]
\label{thm:rational-cover}
\claimid{HC-1}.
Let \(H\) be the rational seven-space of harmonic cubics, and let
\(\mathcal I_{\mathbf Q}\) be the incidence variety of pairs
\(([f],U)\), where \(U\) is a Mukai--Umemura isotropic three-plane and
\(f\perp U\).  The induced extension of
\(\mathbf Q(\mathbf P(H))\) is
\[
 \mathbf Q(\mathbf P(H))\bigl(\sqrt{5J_0}\bigr).
\]
On the Clebsch four-space,
\[
 J_0=16\sigma_3^2,
\]
so over \(D(\sigma_3)\) the cover is the constant golden torsor
\(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q(\sqrt5)\).
\end{theorem}

statements.label: thm:finite-tensor-bridge
statements.title: Finite tensor bridge
statements.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Finite tensor bridge]
\label{thm:finite-tensor-bridge}
\claimid{HC-3}.
There is a \(G\)-equivariant isomorphism
\[
 S:\F_{11}^{\binom{[5]}2}\longrightarrow W
\]
such that, after using the standard pairing to identify the permutation
module with its dual and restricting along
\[
 E(y)_{\{i,j\}}=y_i+y_j,\qquad \sum_i y_i=0,
\]
one has
\[
 E^*(S^{-1})^{\otimes3}T=4\sigma_3.
\]
In particular, the signed matching cubic and the Clebsch cubic span the
same nonzero invariant line over \(\F_{11}\).
\end{theorem}

statements.label: prop:golden-fibre
statements.title: Golden fibre
statements.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Golden fibre]\label{prop:golden-fibre}
\claimid{HC-2}.
Over a field of characteristic different from \(2\) and \(5\), the points
of \(I_t\) lie on \(xyz=0\), have a common nonzero norm, have normalized
squared inner product \(1/5\), and form a six-arc.  The two configurations
over \(\Q\) are therefore defined over
\[
 \Q[t]/(t^2-t-1)=\Q(\sqrt5)
\]
and are exchanged by its nontrivial automorphism.  In Hitchin's normalized
cover of ordered icosahedra they are the complete fibre over \([xyz]\).
\end{proposition}

statements.label: prop:a4-hinge
statements.title: Tetrahedral hinge
statements.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Tetrahedral hinge]\label{prop:a4-hinge}
\claimid{HC-6}.
Let \(G_t=\operatorname{Stab}_{\operatorname{SO}_3}(I_t)\cong A_5\).  Then
\[
 RG_tR^{-1}=G_{1-t},
 \qquad
 G_t\cap G_{1-t}\cong A_4.
\]
\end{proposition}

statements.label: prop:spinor-specialization
statements.title: Spinor specialization
statements.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Spinor specialization]\label{prop:spinor-specialization}
\claimid{HC-4}.
The reduction of \(R\) represents the nontrivial element of
\[
 T_{11}=\operatorname{PGL}_2(11)/\PSL_2(11).
\]
\end{proposition}

statements.label: cor:marked-mathieu
statements.title: Marked Hitchin--Mathieu torsor
statements.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Marked Hitchin--Mathieu torsor]\label{cor:marked-mathieu}
Choose the marking \(I_4\leftrightarrow H_{\rm row}\).  There is a unique
equivariant bijection
\[
 \{I_4,I_8\}\longrightarrow\{H_{\rm row},H_{\rm col}\}
\]
that extends this choice.  It sends \(I_8\) to \(H_{\rm col}\), and
intertwines the reduced Hitchin exchanger with Hadamard row--column
duality.  Without the marking there are exactly two such equivariant
bijections and neither parent is distinguished.
\end{corollary}

statements.label: thm:harmonic-clebsch
statements.title: Harmonic Clebsch bridge
statements.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Harmonic Clebsch bridge]
\label{thm:harmonic-clebsch}
\claimid{PH-1}, \claimid{PH-2}, and \claimid{PH-3}.
Let \(A\) be the Petersen adjacency matrix on the ten face axes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map \(L\) is injective, and its Gram matrix is
\[
 K=\frac1{243}(196I+47J-112A).
\]
Its eigenvalues on
\(\mathbb R^{10}\simeq\mathbf1\oplus V_4\oplus V_5\) are respectively
\[
 \frac{110}{81},\qquad\frac{140}{81},\qquad\frac{28}{81}.
\]
\item Label the axes by the pairs \(\{i,j\}\subset\{1,\ldots,5\}\).
The Clebsch summand is the Petersen \((-2)\)-eigenspace
\[
 a_{ij}=y_i+y_j,\qquad \sum_i y_i=0.
\]
\item For
\[
 F_y(\omega)=\sum_{i<j}(y_i+y_j)P_6(u_{ij}\cdot\omega),
\]
the spherical cubic is
\[
 \frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}F_y(\omega)^3\,d\omega
 =
 -\frac{784000}{1247103}\,\sigma_3(y).
\]
If \(F=\sum_{m=-6}^6q_{6m}Y_{6m}\) in the orthonormal
Condon--Shortley convention and
\[
 W_6(F)=
 \sum_{m_1+m_2+m_3=0}
 \begin{pmatrix}6&6&6\\m_1&m_2&m_3\end{pmatrix}
 q_{6m_1}q_{6m_2}q_{6m_3},
\]
then
\[
 \int_{S^2}F^3\,d\omega
 =-\frac{130}{\sqrt{3553\pi}}\,W_6(F).
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
